international.title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine
international.summary: Bougainville cabinet minister says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’ Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago. Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.
